# Generated by `cafe gen chart` from this project's anywaye.yml.

# identity

The Helm chart identity is deployed from. The templates are the
contract; `values.yaml` is the deployment-time half — the file the
values commit edits.

## The loop

The chart is deployed by ArgoCD, pull-only — and **the Application that
deploys it is not in this repository.** The substrate owns one
Application per service: kit's static manifest
(`kit/templates/substrate/manifests/applications/identity.yaml`) syncs
`oci://ghcr.io/anywaye/charts` / `chart: identity` / `targetRevision:
0.1.0` — the chart's version as the OCI tag. That is the whole of the
deploy path: push a values commit, Argo sees it, the box agrees with
git. A hand edit self-heals; rollback is `git revert`.

`cafe gen chart` still emits `templates/application.yaml` (a **git**
source, `path: chart`), and that file was **deleted** from this chart on
purpose. Two Applications of one name and namespace with different
sources fight, and the later `kubectl apply` wins — a deploy whose
target depends on apply order is not a deploy. The generator's
emission of the file is a cafe-side bug, tracked as the cafe packet that
removes it; this repository deletes the file and does not edit caf.
`internal/chart`'s test asserts the file stays absent.

## Shipping the chart

The chart ships from the fleet's private OCI registry, because the
substrate is closed source and a pull-based system needs somewhere to
pull from:

    helm package chart
    helm push chart-0.1.0.tgz oci://ghcr.io/anywaye/charts/identity

The box pulls it with the read-only secret `values.yaml` names
(`imagePullSecrets`), created on the box once, out of band. The chart
names the secret and never contains a credential.

## Secrets

The service's environment arrives by reference: the Deployment reads
the secret `values.yaml` names (`secretName`) with `envFrom`. Create
it on the box:

    kubectl create secret generic identity-secrets --from-literal=...

Rotate a value by replacing the secret and restarting the pods — not
by editing a generated file.

identity's runtime secrets, every one a NAME in that secret and never
a value in `values.yaml` (enumerated from `internal/config/config.go`,
the one place this service reads its environment):

| Variable | What it is | If it is missing |
|---|---|---|
| `SIGNUP_SIGNING_KEY` | base64url 32-byte HMAC-SHA256 key the signup timestamp is signed under — the second half of signup bot defence | **Startup failure, always.** The one configuration this service must never reach is a signup form with no defence |
| `DATABASE_URL` | the Postgres DSN (embeds the role's password) | Supported state: no pool, readiness is a no-op |
| `OIDC_SIGNING_KEY` | PEM RSA private key the OIDC provider signs id_tokens with | The OIDC block is all-or-nothing and optional — a deployment without it boots a reduced surface |
| `MFA_ENCRYPTION_KEY` | base64url 32-byte key every TOTP secret is sealed under | Supported state: no second factor |
| `COURIER_TOKEN` | identity's credential for courier's introspection endpoint | The courier block is all-or-nothing and optional — no mail path |
| `OAUTH_ENCRYPTION_KEY` | standard-base64 32-byte key OAuth callback tokens are sealed under | The OAuth block is optional — no social login |
| `OAUTH_GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET` | Google social login | That provider is refused at boot |
| `OAUTH_GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET` | GitHub social login | That provider is refused at boot |
| `OAUTH_MICROSOFT_CLIENT_SECRET` | Microsoft social login | That provider is refused at boot |
| `OAUTH_APPLE_PRIVATE_KEY` | the .p8 PEM Apple's client_secret JWT is signed with | That provider is refused at boot |

## The port

The container port is **8080**, and three facts agree on it: the Go
language table `cafe gen chart` reads (the same table `cafe dev` uses),
the Dockerfile's `EXPOSE 8080`, and the Deployment the generator
baked. `internal/chart`'s test asserts the chart's port against the
Dockerfile's, so a chart that drifts from the image it deploys is a red
test rather than a finding somebody reports after a rollout that
routes to nothing.

## Reaching the service

The chart installs an Ingress on `auth.anywaye.com` for identity's
OIDC public face — discovery (`/.well-known/openid-configuration`)
and JWKS (`/.well-known/jwks.json`) answer at the issuer origin.
`ingress.enabled` is `true`, `host` is `auth.anywaye.com`, `path` is
`/` with `pathType: Prefix` matching gateway and parlor. The app-API
surface (`/v1/*`) stays internal and is reached through the gateway
(`api.anywaye.com`); the sign-in form is parlor's page
(`OIDC_LOGIN_UI_URL` says where), not a public surface.

`className` is traefik, k3s's default (DEPLOYMENT.md:28). The
`clusterIssuer` is `letsencrypt-prod`, the ClusterIssuer the
substrate's install step 7 declares (DEPLOYMENT.md, "The ACME solver"
— HTTP-01 through Traefik, no DNS-provider credential); the chart
names it and never creates it. `tls: true` writes the `spec.tls`
block and cert-manager provisions the certificate. Without an issuer
there is no TLS: a secret nothing writes.

## Readiness

The probe is `/readyz`. That is the fleet's contract: every anywaye
service serves it, and the rollout waits on it. It is baked into the
template rather than left as a value, because a readiness path that
can be edited is a readiness path that can be pointed at `/up` — the
defect the kamal template had, which produced deploys that could
never go green. `/healthz` is the other wrong answer: it answers "the
process is up" before the service can serve, so a rollout waiting on
it hands traffic to a container that refuses it.

## The chart's own test

`internal/chart` reads these files off disk and holds them to the
service: the chart's name and version (the seam to the Application's
`targetRevision`), the image tag's seam to the chart version, the
Ingress's off-by-default gate and issuer, the Service port's agreement
with the container port, the container port's agreement with the
Dockerfile's `EXPOSE`, the readiness path, the Service's named
`targetPort`, and the absence of `templates/application.yaml`. It
needs no database.
